sections.h2: Which Fulton County offices handle my tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices share the job. The Board of Assessors sets the value on each parcel, and the Tax Commissioner prints, mails and collects the bill.

According to the Tax Commissioner's own page, that office collects for the county government, the Fulton County and Atlanta school systems, the State of Georgia, and five cities: Atlanta, Mountain Park, Sandy Springs, Johns Creek and Chattahoochee Hills. If your house sits in another Fulton city, expect that city to run its own bill. Every levy appears on its own line because each body picks its own rate.

Fulton stretches across 526.70 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 1,098,791 residents. A house in dense Sandy Springs and one in rural Chattahoochee Hills can land in very different tax situations, so read the parcel on your own bill before relying on any county average.

sections.h2: Where can I visit the tax offices, and when are they open?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner lists several walk-in centers. Four of them post weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the shared phone number on the county page is 404-613-6100.

  • Government Center downtown: 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113, Atlanta 30303.
  • Maxwell Road center: 11575 Maxwell Road, Alpharetta 30022.
  • North Fulton center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Sandy Springs 30350.
  • South Fulton center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, College Park 30349.
  • Greenbriar Mall center: 2841 Greenbriar Parkway, Suite 124, Atlanta 30331.

For valuation or exemption questions, the Board of Assessors takes calls at 404-612-6440 and email at boa@fultoncountyga.gov, with its main office at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018. You can look up and pay a bill at fultoncountytaxes.org, and assessment notices are posted at fultonassessor.org.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 tax year unfold in Fulton County?
sections.html:
It ran on temporary numbers. Notices of assessment appeared online June 19, 2026, and the cutoff to contest a value was Friday, July 31, 2026 for most owners, a date now behind us.

Bills went out August 15, 2026. The state had not yet certified the 2026 digest, so the county asked the Superior Court of Fulton County for a temporary collection order, granted August 4, 2026, and used the 2025 millage rates. The City of Atlanta's share came due September 30, while the county and every other jurisdiction came due October 15. A revised bill or a refund follows only when final rates differ from the temporary ones.

If you plan to sell, find out from the Tax Commissioner whether the parcel carries a temporary or final bill, and have your settlement agent explain how any later adjustment is divided.

sections.h2: What does a Fulton County assessment appeal involve?
sections.html:
The clock is 45 days from the date printed on the notice. Only the assessed value is open to challenge, since the estimated tax amount is off limits.

You can submit online at fultonassessor.org, mail it in, or hand it over at a Board of Assessors office. When you file, you choose one of three routes: the Board of Equalization, non-binding arbitration limited to valuation, or a Hearing Officer. Arbitration and the officer route may involve fees. Plan on several months, and keep paying any temporary bill that arrives meanwhile, because skipped payments add penalties.

The state's property tax FAQ lists the grounds you can raise: taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. It also states that the state revenue agency cannot overrule a local board on a single appraisal.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for homestead relief in Fulton County?
sections.html:
Homestead relief reduces the taxable value of a house you own and occupy. Georgia's baseline exemption is $2,000 of assessed value, and many counties stack larger ones on top.

In March 2026 the assessors announced fresh school-tax exemptions with no income test:

  • Fulton County School District: 25% of assessed value for owners 65 or older as of January 1, rising to 50% at age 70.
  • To qualify there, you must have held a homestead exemption in that district for at least 5 of the last 6 years.
  • Atlanta Public Schools district: as much as $50,000 off assessed value for owners 65 or older as of January 1, combinable with other APS exemptions.

These apply to school levies only. Owners who already have a basic exemption and fit the new criteria get the discount applied without refiling. People who did not own on January 1 apply the next year, and the county confirmed that owners who qualified for 2026 but missed April 1 could apply during the appeal period.

sections.h2: How do I settle the tax bill when selling in Fulton County?
sections.html:
The owner on January 1 carries the whole year's tax. The state revenue agency spells out that Georgia gives no partial refund when someone sells and moves, so any split with the buyer comes from the contract language.

The state's worked formula reads: (assessed value minus $2,000) times the millage rate equals the tax, with assessed value fixed at 40% of fair market value. Fulton's bill breaks the county, school and city rates apart, so check each line.

Before listing, search your parcel on the county tax site and confirm nothing is overdue. County tax liens go on the clerk's general execution docket, and unpaid taxes are best cleared before a sale. If a balance exists, request a payoff amount from the Tax Commissioner and bring it to whoever prepares your settlement statement.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Fulton County housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts reports a median owner-occupied home value of $458,800 for 2020 to 2024, with 54.3% of homes owner-occupied. Median gross rent over that span is $1,732, and the housing stock stood at 534,663 units in July 2025.

Household income has a median of $95,292, and 9,660 building permits were recorded in 2025. Nearly half of occupied homes are rented, so a house with tenants or deferred repairs is a common situation here, and each one changes how a sale and its tax paperwork should be timed.

faqs.q: When does Fulton County collect property tax?
faqs.a: The dates change by year and by jurisdiction. In 2026 the City of Atlanta's share was due September 30 and everything else, including county and school levies, was due October 15. Your own bill prints the date, and the Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100 can confirm it.

faqs.q: What happens if I pay Fulton County tax late?
faqs.a: Interest begins the next day and runs until you pay. A 5% penalty lands on day 120, and another 5% every 120 days after, up to 20%. The office takes partial payments, though interest continues on whatever principal remains.

faqs.q: Can the person who bought my house still appeal the value?
faqs.a: Only the owner named on the notice can appeal, and the notice date starts a 45-day clock. For 2026 that clock ran out July 31 for most owners. If you sell before the next notice, ask your settlement agent who files for that year.

faqs.q: Does the seller or buyer pay Fulton County tax at closing?
faqs.a: The contract divides it. Georgia assigns the full year to the January 1 owner and offers no state refund to a seller who leaves mid-year. The settlement statement shows how your deal handled the split.

faqs.q: How do I get a homestead exemption in Fulton County?
faqs.a: Apply with the Board of Assessors. April 1 is the normal cutoff, and the county said a second window opens during the 45-day appeal period. Buyers who moved in after January 1 apply for the following tax year. Call 404-612-6440 to confirm your case.
